name: Dakar
coordsNote: Plateau (city centre). Long-stay visitors mostly base in Almadies, Ngor and Mermoz, 8–12 km north-west on the same peninsula; climate is near-identical.

US.note: Visa-free up to 90 days; passport valid 6+ months and a yellow-fever vaccination card required.

UK.note: Visa-free up to 3 months; may be asked for onward/return ticket and accommodation proof. Longer stays need a carte d'étranger.

EU.note: Visa-free under 3 months (confirmed for France on 29 Sep 2026); a resident card is needed beyond that.

AU.note: Visa-free up to 90 days per Senegal's exemption list (secondary source); Smartraveller defers to Senegal's embassy — confirm before travel.

english.rationale: Senegal is in EF EPI's low band (score 442; Dakar 459). French and Wolof are the working languages; English is workable in Almadies/Ngor hotels, surf camps and expat businesses but thin elsewhere, so no expat-hub bump.

vibe: Breezy Atlantic peninsula capital: surf breaks, live music, a serious art scene
narrative: A breezy Atlantic peninsula where the Ngor and Ouakam surf breaks, Almadies seafood shacks and the ferry to Gorée Island sit beside a big live-music scene and the Dak'Art contemporary-art biennale. Dry and pleasant November–May, but it is an expensive city for expats, French or Wolof beats English, and robbery along the Corniche after dark is a real concern.

season.rationale: Dry season runs November–May and is the tourist high season; November–February is the coolest and most popular. The rainy hivernage (roughly July–October in Dakar, heaviest August–September) is hot, humid and quiet. Much of Dakar's visitor flow is business/expat, so swings are milder than at a beach resort.

safety.propertyNote: Street robbery (sometimes armed), bag-snatching from scooters, home burglary
safety.womensSafetyNote: Sexual assault rarely prosecuted; women advised not to walk alone, incl. on beaches
safety.touristRationale: Foreigners are specifically targeted at night and on the tourist Corniche; airport extortion and bogus-taxi scams are common.

rationale.property: Editorial estimate: US, UK, AU and French advisories all describe robbery/assault (sometimes armed), motorbike bag-snatching and night-time burglary as common and rising in Dakar, a more violent profile than Marrakech's scams and pickpocketing (55) but far from Cape Town (40); set at 48, near Mexico City (45).
rationale.tourist: 0.95 like Marrakech: the U.S. notes robberies on the Corniche d'Ouest, an area frequented by Westerners; Smartraveller says criminals target foreigners at night and flags airport extortion and unlicensed-taxi overcharging.
rationale.womens: -5 on the country baseline: no advisory singles out harassment of women the way Morocco's do, but Smartraveller says sexual assault is rarely prosecuted and advises against walking alone, including on beaches.

selection: West Africa's most established expat/surf/remote-work city: dry, breezy Nov–May, fills a thin Africa region (two cities today), and gives a winter-sun option a short flight from Europe.
researchNotes: Advisory: Senegal is Level 1 country-wide; only the Casamance region (far south, not Dakar) is Level 2 for crime and landmines, so risks[] is left empty for Dakar (the page's only indicators, Crime and Landmines, are Casamance-specific). travel.state.gov returned a bot check; level/text/date from the official advisory feed (published 2025-11-30T19:00-05:00 = 01 Dec 2025 UTC; RSS pubDate Mon 01 Dec 2025). Other governments are stricter: Smartraveller 'high degree of caution' (unrest + crime), France yellow zone for Dakar. Visa: in Aug 2025 the PM announced a reciprocity-based e-visa; as of 29 Sep 2026 France Diplomatie and GOV.UK still show visa-free stays under 3 months and the U.S. feed shows 90 days, so treated as not implemented — recheck before launch. AU rule is not stated on an official page I could open (Smartraveller defers to Senegal's embassy); recorded as visa-free 90 days from the exemption list (secondary). Yellow-fever card: the U.S. page lists it as required for entry. Homicide override left null: no citable Dakar or regional homicide rate found. Swim: satellite SSTs may run warm near shore in the Feb–Apr upwelling season; months kept conservative. Harmattan hazard may overlap the pipeline's CAMS PM2.5 (dust is included there); kept because the brief calls it out. One-off: the 2026 Youth Olympic Games (31 Oct–13 Nov 2026) will tighten short-let supply in Oct–Nov 2026 only; not listed as an event.
